I've recently heard about TM and it sounds like meditation on spiritual steroids. I'd like to know if any of you have any experience with it. I've heard you have to pay a lot of money to be taught when it only takes an hour to teach TM.
Transcendental Meditation: is it a hoax or does it work?

TM is non-directive style meditation technique. It is a mix between mantra meditation and diaphragmatic breathing. For free, with a little research, you can learn both of these (check youtube).

I would suggest mindfulness meditation over mantra based meditation. In mindfulness you just pick a sensation (usually one associated with the breath- it could even be a mantra though) and return to it every time you are mindful (aware) that the mind is wandering. This is the same general idea as mantra meditation but with more possible sensations to focus on rather than just non-discursive, inner monologue.

The big difference is that in mindfulness you are applying some effort to initially focus the mind and to sustain that focus for as long as possible. In TM (being non-directive) you just sit back and relax. To be honest, the part confuses me some. It seems to me that TM is really just a mindfulness practice where they constantly stress applying no effort even though it actually does take some effort to focus on a mantra. Kind of like if I gave you vanilla ice cream and just kept calling it chocolate over and over. So much so that you caved and decided to call it chocolate too. (I am sure there are people that disagree with that assessment.)

In regards to mindfulness of breathing (or any sensation), if a moment of mindfulness is not enough to return to your anchor (depending on how attached to the thoughts we are, often times it is not), there are 5 different techniques for letting go of thoughts. The buddha outlines them in Vitakkasanthana Sutta: The Relaxation of Thoughts.

Thank you so much for your detailed explanation. I am going to look into it more, but I feel I don't really feel like I'm missing out on anything too special. The meditation I do is working for me, and I just need more practice and more time.

Thanks again.
